title: Jude and the Bell
premise: Sable Eriksen takes a teaching post in the dying town of Harrow's Bend, where a class of students vanished decades ago and the schoolhouse bell rings by itself each October. When every mirror in Sable's rented house begins lagging one second behind reality, they realize the reflections are showing what happens next — and what happens next is the return of whatever the town's founders invited in to guarantee their harvest. As the harvest moon rises, Sable and a ragged found family of students and outcasts must uncover the original bargain, refuse the town's complicit silence, and break the bell before dawn — at the cost of the only home Sable has ever been offered.
about_author: Quentin Iversen is the pen name of a former rural schoolteacher who spent eleven years in towns small enough that everyone knew which houses to avoid after dark. They write horror about institutions, bargains, and the children history forgets.

chapters.title: The Long Road In
chapters.summary: Sable arrives in Harrow's Bend at dusk, counting doors out of old habit, and meets Principal Voss, whose welcome is warm but whose eyes keep drifting to the schoolhouse bell tower. POV: Sable. Beat: uneasy hope — a fresh start that already feels watched.

chapters.title: Twenty-Six Empty Seats
chapters.summary: On Sable's first day, the attendance ledger lists a class of students who haven't existed since 1974, and the current kids go silent when asked about 'the missing class.' A girl named Wren lingers after bell. POV: Sable. Beat: creeping wrongness beneath ordinary routine.

chapters.title: House on Latch Street
chapters.summary: In her rented house, Sable finds a child's chalk drawings behind wallpaper: a bell, a moon, twenty-six stick figures holding hands. The landlady, Mrs. Odum, warns her never to cover mirrors at night. POV: Sable. Beat: domestic dread taking root.

chapters.title: One Second Late
chapters.summary: Brushing her teeth, Sable sees her reflection move a beat after she does. Testing it, she raises a hand; the mirror answers late, then smiles when she doesn't. POV: Sable. Beat: the first undeniable proof — terror sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: Wren Knows the Words
chapters.summary: Wren reveals the kids recite a skipping rhyme about the bell and the harvest moon, passed down like an inoculation. She asks Sable, quietly, if the new teacher is 'on the list.' POV: Wren. Beat: alliance forming; the children know more than the adults admit.

chapters.title: What the Bell Remembers
chapters.summary: Sable researches in the school basement archive: in 1974, the town council 'invited' something to save the failing harvest, and twenty-six students were its payment. The ledger's ink is still wet. POV: Sable. Beat: horror of institutional complicity — power bought with children.

chapters.title: Doors Counted Twice
chapters.summary: Sable begins locking down the house each night, counting doors, taping mirrors. The reflections start arriving early now — showing rooms before Sable enters them. Mrs. Odum is found standing in her own garden, facing the school. POV: Sable. Beat: the haunting escalates from observation to summons.

chapters.title: The Found Family Supper
chapters.summary: Sable hosts dinner for Wren, two other marked students, and the disgraced janitor Deke, who was blamed for the 1974 disappearances. Strangers become a unit over burnt casserole and shared fear. POV: Deke. Beat: warmth against the dark — found family crystallizing.

chapters.title: Voss's Bargain
chapters.summary: Principal Voss privately offers Sable a transfer and a raise if they leave before the full moon, revealing the town renews the invitation every generation and always needs 'a keeper of the count.' POV: Sable. Beat: temptation and moral clarity — the corruption of power made personal.

chapters.title: Reflections of the Missing
chapters.summary: The mirrors begin showing the 1974 class, alive, waving Sable closer. Wren's reflection stops copying her entirely and starts mouthing warnings. POV: Wren. Beat: grief and manipulation — the dead used as bait.

chapters.title: Rhyme Against the Dark
chapters.summary: Deke teaches the group the full skipping rhyme, which encodes the ritual's rules: the bell tolls thirteen times before the harvest moon sets, and the invited thing can be refused by someone who counts it out loud. POV: Deke. Beat: fragile empowerment through inherited knowledge.

chapters.title: The Town That Looks Away
chapters.summary: Sable confronts the town council; they are polite, immovable, and terrified — several bear the same one-second-late blink. Justice here was never legal; it was buried. POV: Sable. Beat: despair at systemic rot, hardening into defiance.

chapters.title: Thirteen Days Out
chapters.summary: Preparations: salt lines, mirrored shards wrapped in black cloth, a plan to reach the bell tower. One student's family flees town in the night, leaving their child behind — with Sable. POV: ensemble via Wren. Beat: stakes narrowing; the family of choice becomes literal.

chapters.title: The Harvest Moon Rises
chapters.summary: The moon crests huge and orange. Every mirror in Harrow's Bend shows the schoolhouse full of light and small shapes moving. The bell gives its first toll. POV: Sable. Beat: point of no return — dread transfigured into purpose.

chapters.title: What Was Invited In
chapters.summary: In the school, the entity wears the faces of the missing class, offering Sable belonging, a home, a family that will never leave — everything they've wanted. It shows them the bargain's fine print: refusal means the town starves. POV: Sable. Beat: the corruption of power aimed at the heart — temptation as horror.

chapters.title: Wren Refuses First
chapters.summary: The entity turns to Wren, promising her absent mother. Wren speaks the rhyme aloud, breaking its hold on herself, and drags Sable back from the edge of acceptance. POV: Wren. Beat: courage of the young — the student saving the teacher.

chapters.title: Count the Doors
chapters.summary: Hunted through shifting corridors where every door leads back to 1974, the group counts doors aloud as living anchors while the bell tolls toward thirteen. Deke is taken by a hallway that wasn't there. POV: Deke. Beat: sacrifice — grief fueling the final push.

chapters.title: The Bell Tower
chapters.summary: Sable and Wren climb the tower as the twelfth toll sounds, the entity climbing the stairs as the missing class, pleading. Sable reaches the bell rope and understands: the bell isn't summoning it — it's holding the door open. POV: Sable. Beat: climax threshold — revelation under maximum pressure.

chapters.title: Thirteen Toll
chapters.summary: Sable refuses to ring the thirteenth toll, speaking the count aloud instead — naming all twenty-six missing children, then the living. The entity, uninvited and unnamed by consent, unravels as the moon sets. The bell cracks. POV: Sable. Beat: cathartic climax — justice spoken outside any law.

chapters.title: Aftermath of Light
chapters.summary: Dawn. Mirrors reflect on time again. The town wakes remembering everything, shame naked in the daylight; the council resigns in pieces. Wren moves into Latch Street with Sable. POV: Wren. Beat: exhausted relief — the cost tallied honestly.

chapters.title: What We Keep
chapters.summary: Weeks later, the school reopens with a memorial wall for the twenty-six. Sable keeps the cracked bell shard on their desk, not as trophy but as promise. Doors get counted once, gently, out of habit. POV: Sable. Beat: quiet healing — vigilance without fear.

chapters.title: The Second Before Sunrise
chapters.summary: Final image: a new mirror in a thrift shop window in another town lags one second late, and a bell somewhere rings twelve times and waits. Sable, driving away with Wren asleep beside them, turns the car around. POV: Sable. Beat: resonant close — the fight for justice never fully ends, but no one faces it alone.
